newsitem.title: UK: S&P ups India foreign currency outlook to postive.
newsitem.headline: S&P ups India foreign currency outlook to postive.

text.p: Standard & Poors said on Tuesday it had revised its foreign currency rating outlook on the Republic of India to positive from stable and has affirmed its BB plus rating on India's long-term foreign currency debt.
S&P also said it assigned its BBB plus long-term local currency rating to India. The outlook on the local currency credit rating is also positive, S&P said in a statement.
"The higher local currency rating reflects India's greater ability to service rupee-denominated debt owing to its powers of taxation and control over the domestic financial system," S&P said.

It said the outlook revision reflected improvements in India's economic performance and external payments position, which should be sustained if targeted fiscal adjustment could accompany the deepening of India's five-year-old reform programme.

"An upgrade in the ratings hinges on sustained reduction of the fiscal deficit, brought about by continued tax reforms and expenditure containment, substantive progress in restructuring state enterprises and continued fiscal discipline," S&P said.

"Political realignments may force a change in political leadership during the next several years but, as demonstrated by the three administrations that have ruled India this year, significant agreement on economic policies across the political spectrum makes this unlikely to derail India's reform strategy," the agency said.
S&P said India's ratings were based on the following.
-- The success of post-1991 reforms of the investment, trade and exchange rate, tax and financial sectors in strengthening economic performance and prospects.
-- Broad political support for extending economic reforms, which minimises the possibility of future reversal of economic policy.
-- Its track record of uninterrupted external debt service, even under periods of severe balance-of-payments pressures, which stands in contrast with that of other BB category sovereigns.
S&P said the ratings were constrained by the following.
-- India's large fiscal imbalances and a large and costly state enterprise sector.
"If not lessened, such fiscal burdens could further impede private sector growth, encourage inflation and strain India's manageable balance-of-payments position over time," S&P said.
"Though India's net external debt to exports has ben cut by half to 144 percent in 1995, its debt service ratio remains moderately high at 28 percent."

"Risk of balance-of-payments pressures is mitigated, however by a current account deficit likely to average only two percent of GDP, a domestic savings rate of 24 percent of GDP, substantial direct and portfolio investments, and conservative debt managemnt policies," S&P said.
